newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Jurors were dismissed today in the case of mass murderer's Fred West's brother, who was being tried on charges of rape, as it was discovered that he had hanged himself overnight. In a grim re-run of his elder brother's suicide John West cheated possible life imprisonment by hanging himself from a beam in the garage of his Gloucester home.
JAPANESE PRICES PUT A RATE RISE ON HOLD
This morning's release of Tokyo consumer price statistics showing an increase of 0.1 percent for November means that an imminent rise in interest rates is unlikely.

Professor Stephen Littlechild, the electricity regulator, is expected to refuse pleas by electricity companies for a delay to the introduction of competition in the domestic electricity market, due to start in April 1998.
Barclays, NatWest and HSBC are among a
group of banks discussing the possible creation of a multi- billion pound market trading in the debt of companies to whom they have made loans.
BASS POISED TO TAKE MMC CHANCE OVER CARLSBERG BUY

Bass has struggled in its negotiations with the Office of Fair Trading over its 200 million stg acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley. The regulator has demanded such great undertakings of the brewing giant that the group may withdraw from the deal, or risk a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

A legal precedent has been set in Japan. The Tokyo District Court found the Shiba Credit Association guilty of sexual discrimination and ordered the company to pay damages for the first time ever after passing over women for promotion.
